All examples, acceptance criteria, and messages use @supports (e.g., "After (auto-fixed to @supports)" blocks, configuration comments, and warning text).
2) Implemented rule and tests target @implements, not @supports: - Rule implementation: src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts - JSDoc header references a different story path: @story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md (this story file does not exist; the real file is ...-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md). - The rule description and behavior are about preferring the consolidated @implements annotation over @story/@req. - Auto-fix builder constructs @implements, not @supports: - const implAnnotation = `@implements ${storyPath} ${reqIds.join(" ")}`; - No occurrences of "@supports" in this file (search_file_content returned 0 matches). - Tests: tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts - Header: "Tests for: docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md" and @story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md. - Invalid test cases check auto-fix output with @implements, e.g.: * Input: @story + @req Output: @implements * Multiple @req lines => single @implements with all REQ IDs. - Tests validate messages with IDs "preferImplements", "cannotAutoFix", and "multiStoryDetected", all phrased in terms of @implements.
3) Behavior vs. story requirements: - Optional warning / REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING & REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY: - Implemented for @implements: * Rule meta.type = "suggestion", meta.docs.recommended = false. * Tests in prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts confirm the rule is NOT present in configs.recommended and configs.strict and can be configured as "warn" or "error" in a flat config. - This satisfies configurability, but the warnings recommend migration to @implements instead of the @supports format described in the story. - Auto-fix Support / REQ-AUTO-FIX & REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX: - Implemented for @implements: * buildImplementsAutoFix(...) collects a single story path and simple @req IDs and returns a fixer that replaces @story/@req with one @implements line. * Tests verify auto-fix for single @req and multiple @req cases, but all use @implements. - No implementation or tests exist for converting to @supports. - Multi-story Detection / REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT: - Implemented: * analyzeComment and hasMultipleStories(storyPaths) detect more than one story path and report messageId "multiStoryDetected". * Mixed @story/@req + @implements triggers "cannotAutoFix" with an explanatory reason. * These behaviors are covered in prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts. - Preserve Order / REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT: - Implemented for @implements: * applyImplementsReplacement uses the original @story line’s prefix (indentation and optional '*') and reinserts the new @implements line at that same index. * It removes only the original @story/@req lines, preserving the rest of the comment. - This preserves JSDoc structure, but again yields @implements, not @supports. - Both Formats Valid / REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION: - Implemented in spirit but not exactly as specified: * When the rule is off (default), it has no effect; legacy @story/@req are validated only by the other rules (valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, etc.). * Even when enabled, the rule only reports when both @story and @req are present; tests mark comments with only @story, only @req, or only @implements as valid. - Quality Standards / REQ-VALID-OUTPUT: - For the implemented path, auto-fix produces @implements lines that pass annotation-format and deep-validation rules (per Story 010.2), but there is no implementation of an @supports tag or any validation for it.
4) Configuration and documentation: - README.md: - Describes `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` as: "Recommends migration from legacy `@story`/`@req` annotations to `@implements` (opt-in; disabled by default ...)". - No mention of @supports here. - user-docs/migration-guide.md: - Section "Optional `prefer-implements-annotation` migration rule" describes migration from @story + @req to @implements. - Example ESLint config uses "traceability/prefer-implements-annotation": "warn". - Text explicitly says: "rewrite eligible `@story` + `@req` combinations into equivalent `@implements` lines". - No occurrences of @supports in this guide (search_file_content found text only for prefer-implements-annotation and @implements).
5) Project-wide checks: - find_files with pattern '*supports*' under src/ returned no files. - search_file_content for '@supports' in src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts returned no matches. - Jest test run (`npm test -- --verbose`) shows the suite "prefer-implements-annotation rule (Story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS)" passing, and there are no tests for an @supports annotation or @supports migration behavior anywhere in the test output.
traceability.notes: The story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md specifies introducing and migrating to a new @supports annotation. The implementation and tests, however, are all built around a migration rule named `prefer-implements-annotation` that converts @story/@req to @implements, with no support for @supports anywhere in the code or tests. The rule and migration guide align with an earlier or alternate design ("MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS"), not the current story. While many behaviors (optional rule, configurable severity, auto-fix for single-story annotations, multi-story detection, preservation of formatting, and documentation) are present, they are implemented for @implements rather than @supports, and the test/story traceability references the wrong story file name. Therefore, not all acceptance criteria of the @supports-based story are satisfied, and the story is not fully implemented as specified.
